blocks.text: The wish

content.value: BUILD the three follow-ups W21's run-secrets tenant wall (D191-D198, #3889, 57c2966e9) unblocked. (1) PRIMARY connectors-secrets-scoped-admin-http (p2, D197 — THE router.ex wave): today /v1/secrets rides a FLAT [:api, :require_admin] pipeline with zero workspace resolution; add the workspace-scoped secrets CRUD surface (scope "/w/:workspace_slug/p/:project_slug" on [:scoped_api, :scoped_admin]) so a workspace admin manages ONLY their workspace's scoped secrets — never the global tier, never another workspace. CRITICAL: guard the workspace-scope input with Ecto.UUID.cast BEFORE threading it into the Secrets scoped read/write functions (the binary_id CastError gotcha — raw non-UUID input raises Ecto.Query.CastError, a 500). Also flip the bp secret.* CLI manifest auth_tier off blanket-admin where the scoped surface applies. (2) connectors-secrets-first-scoped-consumer (p3): the scoped store has NO reader; pick an HONEST first consumer (NOT ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — D110 forbids it; the Cloud runner bypasses run-secrets by D23/D110). If no honest consumer exists without a live dependency, DEFER with evidence. (3) connectors-secrets-aad-binding (p3): upgrade the D196 SQL-only wall to CRYPTOGRAPHIC — bind workspace_id as AAD in the FieldCipher/DataKeys envelope so a row physically moved to another workspace fails to decrypt; red-first swap-attack test. Scope tightly to these three; no other design gates; knob-4 stays D148-blocked. Every slice pins a RED-FIRST protective test.

blocks.text: Direction

content.value: W21 built the wall inside the context layer — a two-tier store with fail-closed scope semantics that nothing outside the module can reach yet. W22 makes the wall REAL in three senses, in strict priority order. FIRST (must land): the workspace admin gets a door — scoped secrets CRUD as the SIXTH sibling of the router's proven /w/:workspace_slug/p/:project_slug scoped-admin blocks (schemas, webhooks, token mint, chat-token mint, media search-admin), never a novel shape. The flat /v1/secrets surface stays byte-identical global-tier admin. Cross-tenant is an opaque 404, garbage input is a 404 via an Ecto.UUID.cast guard (never a 500 CastError), and the red-first test is ws-B's workspace-admin listing/revealing/mutating ws-A's secrets — it must red on a naive passthrough before the gate exists. The bp secret.* manifest auth_tier decision ships in the same slice, following the token.create/access.grant precedent. SECOND (land if the back-compat story is clean): the wall becomes physics — workspace scope bound as AAD in the FieldCipher/DataKeys envelope, so a raw-SQL row swap to workspace B physically fails to decrypt. The D196a proof says the Cloak baseline decrypts a swapped row cleanly: that IS the red test. The central fork to survey before Decide: one-shot re-encrypt migration vs dual-read vs scoped-rows-only AAD (prod's global ingest_token must round-trip through whatever we pick). THIRD (honesty-gated): the first scoped consumer builds ONLY if the survey finds a genuine offline-provable reader (candidates: studio_chat remote_secrets, site-deploy env, webhook signing); otherwise it is DEFERRED with one-line evidence — a manufactured consumer would be worse than none. Quality bar throughout: minimal production diffs, one scoped router block and nothing else in router.ex (the Sobelow line-shift is advisory and pre-classified), disjoint slice file-sets, every fix pinned by a test that reds before it.

blocks.text: Tentative leans (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

items.value: Lean 1 — Reuse SecretController with scope from conn.assigns rather than a parallel controller, IF the sibling precedents share controllers between flat and scoped routes; the resolved-workspace id from ResolveWorkspace is likely already a verified UUID, so the cast guard's load-bearing site may be the CLI/params path — survey pins where raw input can actually reach the scope arg.

Lean 2 — AAD slice touches the ENCRYPTION FORMAT only, not the schema: scoped rows get workspace-bound AAD; the global tier (NULL workspace_id, ingest_token) keeps working — whether by staying on Cloak or by a global sentinel AAD is the survey's call. No new table expected, so no tenancy-catalog edit — but verify.

Lean 3 — First-consumer defaults to DEFER unless studio_chat remote_secrets or site-deploy env is honestly offline-testable reading a workspace-tier secret; a D-entry must name the consumer and why (its AC 1).

Lean 4 — Slice order matters for the shared seam: the scoped read verb (get/reveal with scope) likely lands in slice 1 (the HTTP surface needs it); slice 2, if built, consumes it. Slices stay file-disjoint: router+controller+manifest / secrets crypto internals / consumer module.

blocks.text: Established (evidence-anchored)

items.value: Wall shape confirmed: Secrets threads scope through all 5 public verbs (get/2, reveal/2 opts[:scope], put/3, list/1, delete/2), :global default byte-identical; 3-clause fail-closed scope_secrets/2; two unsafe_fragment upsert arms; get/1 stays global-pinned for ingest_token/0. The scoped read verb slice 2 feared it must add ALREADY EXISTS — no ownership fork between slices 1 and 2.

CastError gap is REAL and unaddressed: only is_binary guards, zero Ecto.UUID.cast in secrets.ex; a non-UUID binary scope flows into where(workspace_id == ^scope) against :binary_id. All FIVE verbs exposed (put via fetch/2 inside do_put — easy to miss). No test exercises garbage scope. BUT no live path reaches it today: SecretController passes no scope, and ResolveWorkspace only ever assigns a DB-resolved %Workspace{} (id always a genuine UUID; sibling TokenController threads it with no re-cast). So the guard is defense-in-depth at the new controller boundary, and its red test must forge a bad conn.assigns value — it cannot be provoked through a real request.

Router door: 5 named sibling blocks (+ docs search-admin, same shape) at router.ex:2146-2213, ALL exactly scope "/w/:workspace_slug/p/:project_slug" + [:scoped_api, :scoped_admin]; none workspace-only. Flat /v1/secrets at 1842-1851 rides [:api, :require_admin], untouched by W21 (D197 confirmed). WebhookController is the controller-reuse precedent: ONE module serves flat+scoped via ScopeHelpers.scope_opts(conn), plus a validate_uuid-before-threading precedent. Shape mismatch: scope_opts returns [workspace_id: ...] while Secrets wants a bare :scope opt — the explicit translation line in the controller is where the Ecto.UUID.cast guard belongs (Barkpark.Repo.uuid_or_nil/1 is the canonical helper).

SecretController.update/2 has NO {:error, :invalid_scope} clause (Secrets.put/3 can now return it) — a required addition once scope threads through; whether FallbackController catches it is UNVERIFIED (verify round). Audit stamping already shipped (log_audit/4 writes workspace_id per D195); the slice-1 trap is reusing flat controller actions unmodified under the scoped route — scope silently stays :global and audit rows lie.

CLI manifest fork is BIGGER than the wish's framing: secret.* = 4 core_cmds auth_tier "admin" on flat paths (capabilities.ex:1418-1465). token.create's scoped_prefix mechanism is INERT — ctx.ScopedMirror is never set true in any production Go path (url.go:39; context.go:16-23; repo-wide grep); the one real scoped-token caller (vercel_cmd.go:545) hand-rolls the URL. A literal in-place tier flip would break the flat-surface byte-identical AC. Real options for Decide: NEW scoped secret verbs with slugs baked into http.path_template (workspace.project-create precedent) vs flipping ScopedMirror on globally (wider blast radius). Survey claim that generic `bp token create` 404s today is PLAUSIBLE, not proven — verify round runs it live.

AAD slice is a cipher-stack migration, not a parameter add: secrets.value rides Cloak (Barkpark.EncryptedBinary → Vault; AAD = hardcoded constant "AES256GCM", read from deps source) — a wholly separate stack from FieldCipher/DataKeys. FieldCipher's actual GCM AAD is the scope STRING; workspace binding is per-(workspace_id, scope) DEK selection (proven isolating: crypto_test.exs:305-322). Zero production callers pass a scope → zero scoped rows exist in prod → option C (scoped-rows-only AAD; global tier stays Cloak byte-identical, no migration, no ALTER) is the only honestly-offline path this wave. Option A (one-shot re-encrypt) touches prod's live ingest_token and is NOT offline-provable; option B (dual-read) has NO Elixir precedent (the Node bpc1|/bpc2| seam is architecture-only). Even C requires pulling value encryption out of the Ecto type into explicit context-level codec for the scoped branch (Content.Encryption chokepoint pattern). Secrets' scope-string convention (e.g. "secret:<ws>" vs constant) is an open Decide item.

Swap-attack red test template proven: Repo.update_all row-move idiom (17 precedents) + crypto_test.exs:305-322 as the post-fix green shape. Assertion-direction subtlety: post-swap the SQL layer LEGITIMATELY serves the row to ws-B — the fix must fail at the CRYPTO layer (decrypt with caller's workspace against ciphertext sealed under ws-A's DEK), never via an SQL check.

First consumer: DEFER with evidence. Exhaustive grep: exactly 2 production callers of Barkpark.Secrets (SecretController; RequireIngestToken via global-pinned ingest_token/0). Every named candidate fails honestly: studio_chat RemoteSecrets is an unrelated in-memory GenServer; site-deploy env is 100% caller-supplied by design; webhook/media signing reads document fields / Application config; github creds are Plugins.Settings (instance-global BY DESIGN, D196c); connectors credentials are walled off by D37/D38; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY forbidden by D110/D23. CONNECTORS EPIC · WAVE 22 · BUILD WAVE · STRATEGIZE · 2026-07-17

Wave 22 — The tenant wall gets doors and crypto: scoped-admin HTTP, AAD binding, first honest consumer

IN FLIGHT — verifying
Survey (14 reports) is digested below. A 6-assignment verify fleet is flying — the LAST explore round before Decide cuts the plan. Then: Decide ratifies D-entries + slice scopes, builders fly. Epic task task-e640bb01fca6ea38 · slices: connectors-secrets-scoped-admin-http (p2, PRIMARY), connectors-secrets-aad-binding (p3), connectors-secrets-first-scoped-consumer (p3, heading to DEFER on survey evidence).

The wish

BUILD the three follow-ups W21's run-secrets tenant wall (D191-D198, #3889, 57c2966e9) unblocked. (1) PRIMARY connectors-secrets-scoped-admin-http (p2, D197 — THE router.ex wave): today /v1/secrets rides a FLAT [:api, :require_admin] pipeline with zero workspace resolution; add the workspace-scoped secrets CRUD surface (scope "/w/:workspace_slug/p/:project_slug" on [:scoped_api, :scoped_admin]) so a workspace admin manages ONLY their workspace's scoped secrets — never the global tier, never another workspace. CRITICAL: guard the workspace-scope input with Ecto.UUID.cast BEFORE threading it into the Secrets scoped read/write functions (the binary_id CastError gotcha — raw non-UUID input raises Ecto.Query.CastError, a 500). Also flip the bp secret.* CLI manifest auth_tier off blanket-admin where the scoped surface applies. (2) connectors-secrets-first-scoped-consumer (p3): the scoped store has NO reader; pick an HONEST first consumer (NOT ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — D110 forbids it; the Cloud runner bypasses run-secrets by D23/D110). If no honest consumer exists without a live dependency, DEFER with evidence. (3) connectors-secrets-aad-binding (p3): upgrade the D196 SQL-only wall to CRYPTOGRAPHIC — bind workspace_id as AAD in the FieldCipher/DataKeys envelope so a row physically moved to another workspace fails to decrypt; red-first swap-attack test. Scope tightly to these three; no other design gates; knob-4 stays D148-blocked. Every slice pins a RED-FIRST protective test.

Direction

W21 built the wall inside the context layer — a two-tier store with fail-closed scope semantics that nothing outside the module can reach yet. W22 makes the wall REAL in three senses, in strict priority order. FIRST (must land): the workspace admin gets a door — scoped secrets CRUD as the SIXTH sibling of the router's proven /w/:workspace_slug/p/:project_slug scoped-admin blocks (schemas, webhooks, token mint, chat-token mint, media search-admin), never a novel shape. The flat /v1/secrets surface stays byte-identical global-tier admin. Cross-tenant is an opaque 404, garbage input is a 404 via an Ecto.UUID.cast guard (never a 500 CastError), and the red-first test is ws-B's workspace-admin listing/revealing/mutating ws-A's secrets — it must red on a naive passthrough before the gate exists. The bp secret.* manifest auth_tier decision ships in the same slice, following the token.create/access.grant precedent. SECOND (land if the back-compat story is clean): the wall becomes physics — workspace scope bound as AAD in the FieldCipher/DataKeys envelope, so a raw-SQL row swap to workspace B physically fails to decrypt. The D196a proof says the Cloak baseline decrypts a swapped row cleanly: that IS the red test. The central fork to survey before Decide: one-shot re-encrypt migration vs dual-read vs scoped-rows-only AAD (prod's global ingest_token must round-trip through whatever we pick). THIRD (honesty-gated): the first scoped consumer builds ONLY if the survey finds a genuine offline-provable reader (candidates: studio_chat remote_secrets, site-deploy env, webhook signing); otherwise it is DEFERRED with one-line evidence — a manufactured consumer would be worse than none. Quality bar throughout: minimal production diffs, one scoped router block and nothing else in router.ex (the Sobelow line-shift is advisory and pre-classified), disjoint slice file-sets, every fix pinned by a test that reds before it.

Tentative leans (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

• Lean 1 — Reuse SecretController with scope from conn.assigns rather than a parallel controller, IF the sibling precedents share controllers between flat and scoped routes; the resolved-workspace id from ResolveWorkspace is likely already a verified UUID, so the cast guard's load-bearing site may be the CLI/params path — survey pins where raw input can actually reach the scope arg.
• Lean 2 — AAD slice touches the ENCRYPTION FORMAT only, not the schema: scoped rows get workspace-bound AAD; the global tier (NULL workspace_id, ingest_token) keeps working — whether by staying on Cloak or by a global sentinel AAD is the survey's call. No new table expected, so no tenancy-catalog edit — but verify.
• Lean 3 — First-consumer defaults to DEFER unless studio_chat remote_secrets or site-deploy env is honestly offline-testable reading a workspace-tier secret; a D-entry must name the consumer and why (its AC 1).
• Lean 4 — Slice order matters for the shared seam: the scoped read verb (get/reveal with scope) likely lands in slice 1 (the HTTP surface needs it); slice 2, if built, consumes it. Slices stay file-disjoint: router+controller+manifest / secrets crypto internals / consumer module.

Survey plan — 14 assignments

• 1. [secrets-store-landed-shape] What EXACTLY did W21 land on origin/main (#3889, 57c2966e9)? Read api/lib/barkpark/secrets.ex, secrets/secret_record.ex, secrets/secret_audit.ex and the W21 migration: every public function signature with its scope arg, the 3-clause fail-closed gate, the two unsafe_fragment upsert arms, whether ANY scoped read/write path already guards scope with Ecto.UUID.cast, and whether get/1 is still global-tier-pinned per D193. WHY: Slices 1 and 2 thread workspace scope into these exact functions and slice 3 re-wraps their value encryption — the plan starts from what actually shipped, not the design text.
• 2. [router-scoped-precedents] Map ALL five scoped-admin precedents in api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex (schemas, webhooks, token mint, chat-token mint, media search-admin): the [:scoped_api, :scoped_admin] pipeline definitions, which plugs resolve workspace/project (ResolveWorkspace / RequireWorkspaceRole — file paths + how the resolved workspace lands in conn.assigns), whether any precedent is workspace-only (no :project_slug), and who passes :scoped_admin (workspace admin vs instance admin — exact role check). WHY: The scoped secrets CRUD block must be a 6th sibling, not a novel shape; the assigns key decides how SecretController receives scope; workspace-vs-project scoping decides the route shape.
• 3. [secret-controller-and-tests] Read api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/secret_controller.ex + its test: how index/show/update/delete call Barkpark.Secrets today, masked-list vs reveal semantics, audit stamping, and what the cleanest scoped variant looks like (same controller reading conn.assigns scope with :global default, vs a separate ScopedSecretController). Also check how sibling scoped controllers (e.g. webhooks) share/split their controller between flat and scoped routes. WHY: Decides slice 1's controller shape and whether the flat surface stays byte-identical (an AC).
• 4. [cli-manifest-auth-tier] In api/.../capabilities.ex (grep 'secret.'): how are bp secret.* verbs declared today (auth_tier admin), what is the token.create / access.grant scoped_admin precedent the task AC cites, how does the Go CLI resolve workspace/project slugs for scoped verbs, and what would 'flip vs scoped-variants-alongside' each look like concretely? Direction

W21 built the wall inside the context layer — a two-tier store with fail-closed scope semantics that nothing outside the module can reach yet.
